aspect: EXAMPLE - nine days in a screening room at Houston
description: Muhanad J. M. Alshrouf, 22, was held nine days in a secondary screening room at George Bush Intercontinental despite entering on a valid immigrant visa after a years-long process, arriving 5 July 2025 to visit his US-citizen father. Advocates said he had no criminal record and had passed background checks by both US and Israeli authorities. His attorney noted CBP's own policy requires processing within 72 hours; no reason was given and he was denied access to counsel. He was released hours after CAIR alerted the press.
energy_note: Nine days in a room, for nothing, with a valid visa.

aspect: EXAMPLE - visas revoked on arrival at SFO
description: Two Palestinian humanitarian activists invited to speak in the Bay Area were held at San Francisco International; a city supervisor said CBP gave no reason for revoking their visas and indicated the men would be sent back.
energy_note: Invited to speak, returned to sender.

aspect: EXAMPLE - detained returning from her honeymoon
description: Ward Sakeik, a Palestinian woman, was detained by ICE while returning from her honeymoon.

aspect: CBP's position is the structural answer
description: CBP states it cannot discuss individual cases and that a visa does not guarantee entry - an officer at the port of entry determines admissibility. That is legally accurate and means the years of process preceding the flight guarantee nothing.
energy_note: Every approval you obtained, overridable at the desk.

aspect: There is a community advisory, which is its own datapoint
description: CAIR issued a precautionary travel advisory to Palestinian-American Muslim travellers following reports of detentions and invasive questioning, specifically referencing those advocating for Palestinian human rights.
energy_note: Your own civil rights body advises caution about coming home.

aspect: There is precedent with a different nationality
description: In January 2020 more than 80 Americans of Iranian descent were held at length in secondary inspection at the Peace Arch crossing, with nearly 300 reportedly affected, including citizens, permanent residents, elderly people and children.
energy_note: The same procedure, a different nationality, five years earlier.
